title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
author: Lewis Carroll
short_summary: A bored girl named Alice follows a talking White Rabbit down a rabbit hole into a strange underground world called Wonderland. There she grows and shrinks after eating and drinking odd things, meets a grinning Cheshire Cat who can vanish at will, and joins a mad tea party hosted by the Hatter and the March Hare. Wonderland runs on its own upside-down logic, and Alice has to keep her head while everyone around her is losing theirs.
extended_summary:
Alice, sitting bored on a riverbank, sees a White Rabbit in a waistcoat pull out a pocket watch and complain that he is late. She follows him down a rabbit hole and falls a very long way into a hall full of locked doors, where a bottle marked DRINK ME shrinks her and a cake marked EAT ME makes her enormous. Her own tears become a pool she has to swim across with a crowd of animals, who dry themselves with a Caucus-race in which everybody wins.

Mistaken for the Rabbit's housemaid, trapped in his house after growing too big, advised by a hookah-smoking Caterpillar on a mushroom, Alice makes her way through a kitchen full of pepper where a Duchess's baby turns into a pig, to a tea party where it is always six o'clock. She plays croquet with a flamingo for a mallet and hedgehogs for balls while the Queen of Hearts orders everyone's head cut off, hears the Mock Turtle's tearful account of his schooldays, and finally attends the trial of the Knave of Hearts, accused of stealing the tarts. As the trial collapses into nonsense Alice grows to her full size, declares the whole court to be nothing but a pack of cards, and wakes on the riverbank with her sister beside her.

questions.prompt: After the Caucus-race, the Dodo announces that everybody has won and all must have prizes. What does Alice end up receiving as her own prize?

options: Her own thimble, handed back to her
A box of comfits all to herself
A ticket back up the rabbit hole
Nothing at all, as she did not run

questions.explanation: Alice hands round comfits from her own pocket until everyone has a prize — and then the animals notice she has none. So the Dodo solemnly presents her with the only thing she has left, her own thimble, and the whole party bows. The prize-giving is exactly as circular as the race was.

questions.prompt: The Hatter explains why his tea party never ends. Why is it always six o'clock where he is?

options: He fell out with Time, who now ignores him
The Queen ordered every clock to be stopped
The March Hare hid all the clocks in the house
The Dormouse sleeps straight through the hours

questions.explanation: The Hatter sang at the Queen's concert; she screamed that he was murdering the time and called for his head. Ever since, Time will not do a thing he asks, so the clock sticks at six — tea-time — and the party simply moves round the table instead of washing up.

questions.prompt: The Caterpillar tells Alice the secret of the mushroom: "One side will make you grow taller, and the other side will make you grow ___."
questions.explanation: The Caterpillar gives no further explanation and crawls away, leaving Alice to work out that a round mushroom has no obvious sides. She breaks off a piece with each hand — and the first nibble sends her chin crashing into her foot.

questions.prompt: Alice carries the Duchess's howling baby out of the peppery kitchen to save it. What happens to the baby in her arms?

options: It turns into a pig and trots away
It grows into a boy and runs off
It changes into a little hedgehog
It vanishes the way the Cat does

questions.explanation: The grunting gets worse until Alice looks down and finds she is carrying a pig, which she sets down with relief and watches trot into the wood. She decides it makes a handsome pig, though it would have been a dreadfully ugly child — one of the book's coolest, oddest jokes.

questions.prompt: Put these moments from Alice's journey through Wonderland in the order they happen.

items: Alice swims across a pool made of her own tears
Bill the Lizard is sent down the chimney after her
A Caterpillar on a mushroom asks her who she is
A cook throws pans about a kitchen full of pepper
Alice plays croquet using a flamingo as a mallet
The Knave of Hearts is put on trial over the tarts

questions.explanation: Wonderland feels random, but Alice's route through it is a straight line: the hall, the pool, the Rabbit's house, the wood, the Duchess, the tea party, the garden, the sea-shore and finally the court. Nothing she meets ever appears twice — except the Cheshire Cat, who turns up wherever he likes.

questions.prompt: Match each Wonderland creature to what it does when Alice meets it.

right: Declares that everybody has won the race
Sits on a mushroom and demands to know who she is
Insists that everything has a moral in it somewhere
Weeps while listing the lessons he had at school

questions.explanation: Every adult Alice meets is certain and useless at the same time. The Dodo has authority but no answer, the Caterpillar asks the hardest question in the book, the Duchess squeezes a moral out of anything, and the Mock Turtle cries over a school nobody could have attended.

questions.prompt: Alice changes size again and again. Sort each of these by what it does to her.

options.label: Drinking from the bottle marked DRINK ME
Holding the White Rabbit's fan too long
Eating one of the pebbles turned to cakes
Eating the little cake marked EAT ME
Nibbling the left-hand piece of mushroom
Sitting in the courtroom during the trial

questions.explanation: Alice spends the whole book being the wrong size, and only twice chooses it on purpose. The fan is the frightening one — she shrinks without knowing why and drops it just in time. By the trial she has stopped minding, and grows without eating anything at all.

questions.prompt: At the trial the Queen announces: "Sentence first — verdict afterwards." Why does Alice object to this?

options: The punishment would come before deciding guilt
The jury is made up entirely of small animals
The Knave was not in the courtroom to hear it
The tarts had already been eaten by that point

questions.explanation: The Queen's order puts the ending of a trial before its beginning, which would make the whole thing pointless. Alice, who has politely put up with far stranger things all day, finally says "Stuff and nonsense!" out loud — this is the rule she will not accept.

questions.prompt: All through Wonderland Alice tries to stay polite, even when creatures are rude, contradict her or shout at her. At the trial she finally stops and tells the whole court they are nothing but a pack of cards. Was she right to stop being polite at last, or should she have kept her manners? Give your reasons.
questions.explanation: Both sides can earn full marks. A strong 'yes' answer notices that politeness had got her nowhere, that the court was about to punish someone for nothing, and that Alice only speaks out when something actually matters. A strong 'no' answer notices that her outburst ends Wonderland, that she could simply have walked away, or that shouting is no better than the Queen's own behaviour. Accept any answer that gives a reason connected to the trial.

questions.prompt: At the Mock Turtle's school the lessons were Reeling and Writhing, and the classes got one hour shorter every single day. Invent one more lesson for a Wonderland school. What would it be called, and what would the pupils actually have to do in it?
questions.explanation: There is no single right answer. A strong answer invents a lesson that twists a real school subject the way Carroll does — a name that sounds like a real subject gone wrong, plus something the pupils would do. Any invented lesson with an activity attached earns full marks; a bare name with nothing to do in it is thinner.

questions.prompt: Suddenly, at the tea party, the Hatter asks Alice a riddle: "Why is a raven like a ___?"
questions.explanation: Nobody ever answers it. Alice thinks she can guess, the Hatter admits he has not the slightest idea, and the conversation moves on — the riddle is famous precisely because Carroll left it with no solution at all.

questions.prompt: The White Rabbit finds Alice standing outside his house and immediately starts giving her orders. Who does he think she is?

options: Mary Ann, his housemaid
The Duchess's own cook
A gardener from the palace
A messenger from the Queen

questions.explanation: He sends her indoors to fetch his gloves and fan without once looking at her properly. Alice obeys, which is how she gets trapped in the house after growing too big — in Wonderland nobody ever asks who Alice really is except the Caterpillar.
